fact: Then-Lands Minister Jinapor said in 2024 that ELIS had enabled selected services, including consolidated searches and plan approvals, to be completed online, with full migration from manual operations still in progress.
Then-Lands Minister Jinapor said in 2024 that ELIS had enabled stamp duty assessment to be completed online.
Lands Minister Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah said in August 2025 that the Commission's ongoing ELIS digitization would eliminate manual inefficiencies and reduce corruption.

A digital Client Service Access Unit inaugurated in Ho on 3 June 2026 enabled deployment of the Enterprise Land Information System in the Volta Region, where clients can submit land applications and track progress.

Ghana News Agency quotes the Lands Commission's Executive Secretary saying ELIS is operational in Greater Accra and nine other regions, cutting official land searches from about a month to seven working days.

Graphic Online reports that on 15 July 2026 the Lands Minister said the Enterprise Land Information System is operational in nine regional offices, with digital processing of the commission's major services in those regions.

The Lands Commission says its Enterprise Land Information System (ELIS) is a unified workflow-based platform automating its re-engineered processes, with an online portal for searches, registration, transfers and mortgages, while naming incomplete deployment and manual processes alongside digital as gaps.
The Lands Commission's corporate portal lists stamp duty assessment among the services available through its online system.

Ghana News Agency reports that on 2 September 2025 President Mahama told the Lands Commission to integrate services across its Registries, Valuation and Survey departments, building on the enterprise land information system; in-service use of the system is not stated.

Dr Benjamin Quaye of the Lands Commission says the Enterprise Land Information System provides registration, searches and stamping, and industry players can search online without visiting the Commission.
